text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: sustained 5xx spike observed in europe-south1 (eus1) egress gates. Metric: eus1-egress-gw-2 route-queue-depth > 80% for 3m; downstream 503/504 increase on /v1/generate  — Pager: https://pd.example/INC-23345

bob_oncall: ack. I’m oncall and looking. which customers are impacted?

alice_sre: seeing flows to external peer peering-eu-south1-1 sporadically flapping; BGP withdraws followed by reconnects. early guess: egress peer saturation + NAT pool exhaustion causing 502s.

carlos_net: confirming, NAT translations for eus1-eips at 95% in the last 10m. raising rate-limit on ephemeral allocations won’t help. running quick health: `curl -s -I https://eus1-egress-gw-2.internal/status` shows 503 intermittently.

bob_oncall: ok, mitigation plan: 1) divert new requests away from eus1 to eu-west1/eu-north1 via smart-routing policy, 2) drain node pool on eus1-egress-gw-2, 3) open customer comms draft. doing step 1 now.

frank_engineer: executing routing change. patch to routing tier:
```bash
# increase fallback weight for eu-west1 + eu-north1
routectl set-policy smart-routing --region-priority eus1:0,eu-west1:1,eu-north1:1 --reason "egress saturation eus1"
```
Applying...

IncidentBot: system: routing policy apply job queued (job id j-9f3a). ETA ~30s.

alice_sre: while routing shifts, we should also reduce connection churn from long-lived backoffs. increasing prefix-KV cache TTL for eus1-serving to 30s to avoid rewarming. doing config push.

frank_engineer: routing job succeeded. traffic diversion starting. I see 60% of new connections forced to eu-west1, 30% to eu-north1; eus1 accepted residual pinned sessions only.

bob_oncall: observability — can we get a quick dashboard blip? ellie_pm can you paste the link for the public status page edit?

ellie_pm: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/edit/23345 — draft below for review:  

DRAFT - Status page (please edit):
"We are investigating elevated error rates for a subset of requests originating from Europe (europe-south1). Customers may see increased 502/503 responses for the hosted API. We have implemented an automated traffic diversion to alternate regions (eu-west1 and eu-north1) while we remediate the egress saturation. Customers pinned to europe-south1 may see increased latency. Next update: in 30 minutes or as events progress."

dana_comm: copy edit: change "pinned to europe-south1" -> "using regional pinning to europe-south1"; add severity header and suggested customer action: retry with exponential backoff. Also add contact line for enterprise customers.

bob_oncall: good. dana_comm, can you prepare the customer notification (short) for affected customers + expanded enterprise template? we want to send minimal notice now (informational) and a follow-up with RCA later.

dana_comm: draft customer DM: 
"We’re currently mitigating an elevated error rate affecting requests routed through Europe (europe-south1). We’ve implemented region-level routing diversion to reduce impact; some customers with region pinning may observe higher latency. Our engineers are actively monitoring — ETA for broad recovery is 30-60 minutes. If you have contractual SLAs, reply to this thread and we’ll escalate."

alice_sre: quick config/log snippet from eus1 gateway: 
```log
[2026-03-15T12:05:12Z] eus1-egress-gw-2 nat_map_full=true trans_alloc=95%
[2026-03-15T12:05:14Z] connection-reset client=10.8.2.34:443 -> upstream=203.0.113.5:443 503
[2026-03-15T12:06:01Z] route-queue-depth=82%
```
This matches NAT pool exhaustion.

frank_engineer: draining nodes in eus1-egress-gw-2 now: `k8s drain eus1-egress-gw-2 --grace-period=30s --ignore-daemonsets` — will trigger new connections to go to fallback regions faster.

IncidentBot: Pager duty: bob_oncall acknowledged, handoff scheduled in 40m to alice_sre.

bob_oncall: update: after routing shift + node drain, 503 rate dropped from 12% -> 2.1% within 120s for /v1/generate. Latency increased ~40-80ms for rerouted traffic. Monitoring for error regression.

dana_comm: I posted the status page draft. Ready to send customer DM to the affected bucket once we confirm impact window. Suggest sending a short notice now: "We are actively mitigating; diversion in place; monitoring."

ellie_pm: flagging customers with region pinning active in eus1: customer list size ~14 orgs, high-volume subset 3 orgs. recommending direct outreach to the 3.

carlos_net: longer term fix: reclaim NAT space or add additional egress elastic IPs to eus1 or adjust peering to increase capacity. but immediate fix done.

bob_oncall: agreed. will open follow-up ticket for NAT scaling and peering ops. ticket: OPS-4589.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: scheduled on-call handoff to alice_sre in 40 minutes.

frank_engineer: monitoring graphs show error rate trending down to baseline; still some flapping on low-volume flows. keeping drains for 10 more minutes.

dana_comm: sent initial customer DM to affected list (short notice). will prepare enterprise-specific patch for contractual customers.

bob_oncall: 15m pass update for internal channel: 
- What happened: NAT exhaustion on eus1 egress nodes causing elevated 5xx for hosted API traffic.
- Impact: ~10% of requests from region, 14 customers affected (3 high-volume).
- Mitigation: traffic diversion to eu-west1/eu-north1; drained affected nodes; increased KV cache TTL; monitoring.
- Next steps: add egress EIPs to eus1, update peering, RCA.

alice_sre: confirm: we should rotate this thread to postmortems after stabilization. creating incident stub: INC-23345-PM in tracker.

frank_engineer: final: error rate down to 0.4% for /v1/generate in eus1, latency stable. routing diversion removed (resumed normal weighting) and nodes uncordoned.

bob_oncall: closing active mitigation. leaving incident open for RCA and customer follow-up. final internal note: team kudos for quick routing change and comms. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: incident state changed -> mitigated. Auto notify: status page updated to "Mitigated - monitoring" and customer DM sent.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff to alice_sre started.

frank_engineer: downstream action items created: OPS-4589 (egress capacity), ENG-7732 (automated NAT scaling), COMMS-211 (customer follow-up).

bob_oncall: thanks everyone. I’ll compile the timeline and hand over to alice for RCA continuation.

alice_sre: acknowledged. I’ll pick up RCA and post updates to #postmortems in 48h.

(End of thread)"
